prior_year_events.impact_description: material exposure to motor casualty claims through motor treaty policies written on the 2014 and prior years of account

The calculation of these outstanding claims is informed by the discount rate used in determining lump sum awards in personal injury cases referenced in the Ogden tables, which is currently at 2.5%. This rate is currently under review by the Lord Chancellor and an updated rate is expected to be announced as early as February 2017, which increases the uncertainty of the Syndicate's total reserves.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate reported a gross release of GBP 19.13m from prior year reserves in 2016, contributing to a net release of GBP 57.6m. This was primarily driven by more favourable claims development than originally anticipated and proactive claims management. The syndicate also noted material exposure to motor casualty claims from 2014 and prior years, with uncertainty surrounding the Ogden discount rate review. The 2016 year was impacted by the Alberta wildfire and Hurricane Matthew, incurring net losses of GBP 12.0m and GBP 5.9m respectively.

data.data_quality_notes: The narrative text on page 2 and 14 states a net release of GBP 57.6m. However, the Technical Provisions note on page 15 explicitly shows a gross movement in provision of -GBP 19.13m. The gross figure from the Technical Provisions note is used as per instructions. The claims development table is distorted by the acceptance of Syndicate 1400's RITC for the 2013 year of account and cannot be used to reliably derive gross PYD.
